equityFacts: [FACT — Hero equity vs the modeled villain range(s), computed on-device by Monte Carlo (10000 trials), NOT by you: pre-flop ~50%, flop ~83%, turn ~61%, river ~14%. These are deterministic ground truth — your assessment of each street MUST be consistent with them. The modeled villain ranges already include a GTO-balanced share of bluffs, so this is hero's true bluff-catch equity — compare it directly to any pot-odds price FACT (whether labelled "Price for hero to call" or "Price hero was getting when he folded") to decide call vs fold. A low number means hero loses to most of villain's range and is at best a weak bluff-catcher.]

[FACT — Villain MrPink (UTG) range behind the equity above: Pre-flop: open-raised → UTG opening range (~5% of hands); Flop: bet (~106% pot) → polarized: top 30% value + bottom 15% bluffs; Turn: bet (~136% pot) → polarized: top 30% value + bottom 15% bluffs; River: bet (~64% pot) → polarized: top 30% value + bottom 11% bluffs.]

[HEURISTIC — Equity REALIZATION (raw equity discounted for hero's position + hand class; ESTIMATED, not exact): flop ~83% → realized ~93% (OOP, a strong made hand); turn ~61% → realized ~68% (OOP, a strong made hand); river ~14% → realized ~16% (OOP, a strong made hand). A marginal hand out of position rarely realizes its raw equity; a strong made hand over-realizes. Weigh the continue / bluff-catch read against the REALIZED figure, not the raw one — but this is heuristic context: a decisive pot-odds price FACT and the hard equity FACT above still take precedence.]

[HEURISTIC — SPR & COMMITMENT (effective stack ÷ pot, hero-centric; ESTIMATED, not exact): flop SPR ~20.8 — to get all-in profitably needs ~49% equity (high SPR — favours pot control with one-pair hands); turn SPR ~6.3 — to get all-in profitably needs ~46% equity (high SPR — favours pot control with one-pair hands); river SPR ~1.3 — to get all-in profitably needs ~36% equity (low SPR — favours stacking off strong made hands). Use this for the call-vs-raise / stack-off decision, NOT the bluff-catch call (pot odds govern that): at low SPR a strong-enough made hand should commit, at high SPR a one-pair hand favours pot control. With a marginal made hand villain's stack-off range skews to sets/two-pair, so require more than the raw %. The stack-off % is the equity to get all-in profitably versus a willing range, NOT hero's pot-odds price. This is heuristic context — a decisive pot-odds price FACT and the hard equity FACT still take precedence.]
